fact_text: PTCL describes itself as Pakistan's largest integrated telecom group, running three distinct businesses: fixed-line and broadband, mobile through Ufone, and microfinance banking through U Microfinance Bank.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fixed-line and broadband is PTCL's oldest and still most profitable segment; PTCL provided Pakistan's first broadband connection over DSL when the internet arrived in the country.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Flash Fiber, PTCL's fibre-to-the-home service, is the growth engine of its broadband business and offers faster, more stable and more reliable internet than DSL.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Revenue from Flash Fiber subscribers rose about 50% in 2025, as reported in PTCL's full-year 2025 results.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PTCL's fixed-line and broadband segment operating profit rose almost 50% in 2025 compared with 2024, making it the core foundation of the group's business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PTCL's combined operating profit for 2025 more than doubled versus the prior year, which the analyst presented as early evidence of a turnaround.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PTCL's gross profit was about PKR 9.7 billion in Q4 2025, up from PKR 9.4 billion the prior quarter and PKR 8.3 billion two quarters earlier, which the analyst linked to fibre subscriber growth and a better service mix.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PTCL's operating margin improved from about 14% to about 20% over the last two quarters, which the analyst attributed to tight control of administrative and selling expenses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PTCL's quarterly revenue of about PKR 30.5 billion in Q4 2025 was roughly flat on the prior quarter; the analyst noted possible seasonality but still read the overall trajectory as growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Etisalat took a stake in PTCL in 2006 during the privatisation of the company, which at the time was a flagship privatisation in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PTCL agreed in December 2023 to buy Telenor Pakistan through a share purchase agreement, and the deal completed on 31 December 2025 after regulatory approvals.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Telenor acquisition was reported at about USD 400 million and was partly financed by a seven-year loan from a lender consortium led by the IFC.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Telenor Pakistan's results are to be consolidated into PTCL's reporting from 2026 onward, so the combined figures will show the effect of the merger.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argued that synergies from the Telenor deal, mainly tower and admin cost savings, should exceed the deal's annual financing cost, supporting net profitability for the group from 2026.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Telenor deal is debt-funded, so the analyst treated its financing cost as a drag that the merger synergies must outrun before earnings improve.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Analyst projections put the combined PTCL and Telenor revenue at about PKR 250 billion in 2026 and about PKR 260 billion in 2027, driven by a larger subscriber base; these are assumption-based scenarios.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Analyst estimates put the group's gross profit at about PKR 85 to 90 billion in 2026, up from roughly PKR 40 billion in 2025, and possibly above PKR 90 billion in 2027.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The merged group inherits Telenor's tower company, giving about 19,000 towers, of which management plans to retire about 7,000 overlapping towers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Management estimates that retiring the overlapping towers will save about PKR 21 billion a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ufone, PTCL's mobile subsidiary, sells voice calls, 4G data, SMS, prepaid and postpaid SIMs, data bundles, international roaming and mobile financial services such as the UPaisa wallet and mobile insurance.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argued that acquiring Telenor's subscriber base gave Ufone a scale it could not realistically build organically, which he estimated would take a decade or more.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Combining Ufone with Telenor Pakistan would give the merged mobile operator a market position close to Jazz's, according to the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ufone's 2025 annual report showed estimated revenue of about PKR 106 billion but still a net loss of about PKR 9 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ufone's operating result swung from a loss of about PKR 4.5 billion in 2024 to an operating profit estimated at roughly PKR 6 to 7 billion in 2025.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ufone's bottom line stays under pressure because depreciation, finance costs and spectrum-related expenses sit below its operating profit, so the net result is still a loss.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: U Microfinance Bank, part of PTCL's group, targets unbanked and underbanked customers with micro loans, agricultural finance, savings accounts, branchless banking and digital payments.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Paired with Ufone's UPaisa wallet, the microfinance bank gives the PTCL group a telecom-to-banking ecosystem that could become a competitive edge as digital banking matures in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When an industry shrinks from five major players to three, the price-war model tends to shift gradually toward a price-power model, and industry margins can then improve.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Merging telecom operators cuts cost through overlapping retail shops, consolidated distribution channels and field teams, and duplicate back-office functions such as HR, finance and IT.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After India's telecom market consolidated around 2016 from more than ten operators to three major players, Airtel's EBITDA margin rose from about 47% in 2019 to about 65% in 2025.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over the same period after consolidation, Airtel's average revenue per user roughly doubled, the analyst noted, showing profitability improving alongside pricing power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: ARPU is average revenue per user per month, the core revenue-per-subscriber metric used to judge how much a telecom operator earns from each customer.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Consolidation tends to lift telecom ARPU over time when price competition eases, provided economic growth is not eroded by currency devaluation, which then drives revenue and profitability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's total telecom sector revenue passed PKR 1 trillion for the first time in 2025 per the regulator's annual report, growing about 12% year on year, with subscribers above 200 million.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Rising data demand in Pakistan is the argument for PTCL benefiting, particularly through its fibre broadband and combined mobile network, as broadband connections grow toward 150 million.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan held a 5G spectrum auction in March 2026 in which about 480 of roughly 600 MHz were sold, raising close to USD 500 million for the government.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the March 2026 auction, Jazz won about 190 MHz, Ufone about 180 MHz and Zong about 110 MHz of spectrum.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After the March 2026 spectrum auction, Pakistan's standing in global telecom markets moved up to seventh from fourteenth, per the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Taxes on mobile card loads take a large share of each top-up, so a customer receives far less airtime balance than the amount loaded; the analyst argued this burden should ease gradually for the sector to grow.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How Pakistan's Biggest Telecom Lost 93% of Its Value in 20 Years. Can It Make a Comeback?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
